subject: AtlasOps case study — permission to cite ISO/SOC attestation
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@atlasops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasOps case study — permission to cite ISO/SOC attestation

Hi Sara,

Hope youre doing well — thanks again for the demo last month. Were lining up the case study draft for AtlasOps and would like to include a short compliance blurb referencing Redwoods current public attestations (SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001) alongside the product outcomes.

Two asks:
- Would AtlasOps be comfortable with Redwood including a 1par customer quote that references both product impact and the fact that you reviewed our SOC2/ISO statements?
- Do you have any contractual or PR/legal constraints around language (for example, excluding auditor name or exact attestation dates)?

If youre okay in principle we can send a oneline draft quote and a short permission PDF for signature — happy to route through DocuSign if thats easier. Our target publish window is the first week of August; if that timeline is tight please let me know.

Thanks,

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

From: Sara Lang <sara.lang@atlasops.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasOps Legal <legal@atlasops.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasOps case study — permission to cite ISO/SOC attestation

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for reaching out — were supportive of a case study in principle. A couple of legal/PR constraints to flag up front:
- Please do not publish our internal audit firm or the specific audit dates.
- Any quote that references our compliance posture needs signoff from our legal team (ccd).

If you can send over a proposed oneline blurb and the short permission form well route internally. We can typically turn back approval within 48 business hours once we have those items.

Appreciate you checking.

—Sara
Sara Lang
Head of Partnerships
AtlasOps
sara.lang@atlasops.com

Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700

(Forwarding original outreach; see thread above.)

Vivek here — quick internal note: Marissa, can you draft the customerfacing blurb well send Sara? Laura, please review for any PR concerns. David, would you confirm if the proposed wording is legally safe (specifically around claiming certification vs. attestation and avoiding auditor name/dates)?

Im attaching a rough starter blurb (draft_blurb_v0.txt). Goal is to keep it to one sentence the customer can approve quickly.

Thanks — Vivek

Attachment: draft_blurb_v0.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasOps case study — legal blurb draft & attestation wording

Thanks Vivek — attached is a suggested customerfacing blurb and a slightly longer paragraph we can offer as optional context. I kept the wording highlevel per Saras note (no auditor, no dates). Please review and flag any legal/PR changes.

Proposed 1line blurb (for signoff):
"AtlasOps reduced inference latency by 3x using Redwood Inference while maintaining our security and compliance posture; Redwoods current public attestations include SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001."

If legal is ok with this phrasing Ill send to Sara as a followup and attach a simple permission PDF for signature.

Attachment: redwood_blurb_v1.txt

—Marissa Cole
Customer Marketing
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sara Lang <sara.lang@atlasops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasOps Legal <legal@atlasops.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasOps case study — legal blurb draft & attestation wording

Hi Marissa and Vivek,

Thanks — that oneline reads well and is acceptable with a small edit: please remove the explicit mention of "ISO 27001"; were fine referencing "Redwoods public attestations" but prefer not to name the standard in the body copy for this case study. Otherwise we approve.

Ive signed the permission form and sent it back (attached: AtlasOps_CaseStudy_Consent_20250722.pdf) and also executed via DocuSign here: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/abc123-atlasops-case-study.

Final approved blurb (per AtlasOps legal):
"AtlasOps reduced inference latency by 3x using Redwood Inference while maintaining our security and compliance posture; Redwoods public attestations were reviewed as part of our evaluation."

Please proceed with the draft and share the final onepage case study so we can sign off on the layout and logo usage.

Best,

Sara Lang
Head of Partnerships
AtlasOps
sara.lang@atlasops.com

Attachment: AtlasOps_CaseStudy_Consent_20250722.pdf
